text:
### Observed differences

- The dominant difference is a reversal between two alternative activity groups after A20. In the earlier window, A21, A22 and A23 each ran in about 75 in 100 traces (about 150 of 200) while A24, A25 and A26 each ran in about 25 in 100 (about 50 of 200); in the later window, A21–A23 each appear in only about 25 in 100 traces (49 of 200) and A24–A26 in about 75–76 in 100 (151–152 of 200). Each of the six shifts is roughly 50 percentage points with empirical strength 0.995. [OCC021, OCC022, OCC023, OCC024, OCC025, OCC026]
- A20 itself still runs in essentially every trace, and its outgoing transitions flipped accordingly: before, roughly 75 in 100 of its outgoing transitions went to A21, A22 or A23 and about 25 to A24, A25 or A26; in the later window, roughly 24 in 100 go to A21–A23 and about 75 to A24–A26. [DIR020, POS002]
- The two groups still behave as mutually exclusive alternatives with unchanged placement: A21–A23 still co-occur with A20 and follow it whenever they run, A24–A26 likewise, the two groups almost never share a trace in either window, and the activities' median positions stay around 0.67–0.70 of the trace in both windows. This indicates a change in how often each existing branch is taken, not activities being added, removed or moved. [REL011, REL014, REL022, REL041, POS003, POS006]
- A10 became about four times as common: about 6 in 100 traces before (11 of 200) versus about 21 in 100 in the later window (42 of 200), with occurrences sitting later in the trace (mean relative position about 0.57 before, 0.82 after). In the later window about 90 in 100 of A10's outgoing transitions lead to A33, whereas before its few outgoing transitions were spread over several activities; A10 now typically runs after A20, A30 or A32. [OCC010, POS001, DIR010, REL001, REL008, REL009]
- Some rare activities became rarer: A02 fell from about 9 in 100 traces (18 of 200) to about 1 in 100 (2 of 200), A06 from about 7 to about 2.5 in 100 (14 → 5), and A08 from about 7.5 to about 3 in 100 (15 → 6). A02's outgoing profile also changed completely, but that rests on only two after-window transitions. [OCC002, OCC006, OCC008, DIR002]
- Several activities (A17, A18, A27, A31, A32, A33) show small participation shifts of roughly 2–5 percentage points with only moderate empirical strength (about 0.6–0.75), i.e. within the range random re-splits of an unchanged process produce. [OCC017, OCC018, OCC027, OCC031, OCC032, OCC033]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the hypothesis that the two alternative paths after A20 swapped how often they are taken: the branch through A21, A22 and A23, executed in about 75 in 100 cases in the earlier window, was executed in about 25 in 100 in the later window, while the branch through A24, A25 and A26 rose from about 25 to about 75 in 100, with A20 itself unchanged. [OCC021, OCC024, DIR020]

The change is shown directly at the branching point and consistently across indicator families: A20's outgoing shares mirror the participation swings, both groups still follow A20, still exclude each other, keep their within-group co-occurrence and their trace positions, and each group still runs in a substantial minority/majority of traces in both windows — which rules out the activities having been added, removed, made optional/mandatory, or relocated. The many relation items restate one underlying trace behaviour and are not independent confirmations. [REL011, REL014, REL022, REL041, POS003, POS006]

An important competing explanation the evidence cannot rule out is that the mix of cases entering the process shifted between the windows, so that unchanged routing produced different branch frequencies; the within-process evidence cannot separate this from a modified routing rule. [OCC021, OCC024, DIR020]

Other differences: A10's participation rose from about 6 to about 21 in 100 traces with a later typical position and a now-dominant transition to A33 — a separate participation change the evidence does not tie to the branch reversal [OCC010, POS001, DIR010, REL001]. A02, A06 and A08 became rarer, though each rests on few observations [OCC002, OCC006, OCC008].
